name: Great Scientists
description: The people whose discoveries changed how we understand the world, from Archimedes and Newton to Curie, Einstein and Hawking.

checkpoints.name: The ancient world
checkpoints.note: Greek thinkers look for rules behind nature. Pythagoras and Euclid shape mathematics, Hippocrates medicine and Archimedes mechanics, and Ptolemy's picture of the heavens lasts for fourteen centuries.

checkpoints.name: Scholars of the Islamic world
checkpoints.note: In Baghdad and Cairo scholars preserve Greek science and add to it. Al-Khwarizmi gives algebra its name and Ibn al-Haytham studies light by experiment.

checkpoints.name: The Scientific Revolution
checkpoints.note: Copernicus puts the Sun at the centre, Galileo turns a telescope to the sky, Kepler finds the shape of the orbits and Newton explains them with gravity.

checkpoints.name: Chemistry, evolution and electricity
checkpoints.note: Lavoisier makes chemistry a science of measurement and Mendeleev orders the elements. Darwin explains how species change, Pasteur shows that germs cause disease, and Faraday and Maxwell uncover electromagnetism.

checkpoints.name: Atoms, relativity and DNA
checkpoints.note: Radioactivity, the quantum and relativity change physics within thirty years. Later come the atomic bomb, the computer, the structure of DNA and new pictures of the universe.
